properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 2:15PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds have caused river levels on the St
Johns at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is
forecast to continue to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage
early this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 3.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EDT Sunday was 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.7 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 25 at 6:41PM MDT until October 25 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...

* Until 715 PM MDT.

* At 641 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 17 miles southeast
of Tinnie, or 34 miles southeast of Ruidoso, moving northeast at 15
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Sunset.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 25 at 1:27PM MST until October 26 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Little Colorado River from earlier
excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Birdsprings to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MST /1000 AM MDT/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring near
Birdsprings. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 111 PM MST /211 PM MDT/, water levels have fallen below action
stage at Winslow and will continue to fall this afternoon.
However, downstream impacts will continue near Birdsprings
through Monday morning.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 1:00pm MST /2:00pm MDT/ the stage was 16.94 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels have fallen below action stage and will
continue to fall through this afternoon.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Birdsprings will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow.

- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.
